questions.explanation: Arrow labels never fall through, eliminating the declaration hazard entirely. This is the modern, clean fix.

questions.subject: JAVA_PROGRAMMING
questions.topic: A Matched Case Can Fall Into Default
questions.learningObjective: Use break to stop fall-through into default
questions.stem: In a multi-step plan, switch (x) { case 1: print("one"); break; default: print("def"); } with x=1, what prints?

options.text: Nothing because break cancels the print.

questions.explanation: break after "one" exits the switch, so default does not run. Only "one" prints.

questions.subject: JAVA_PROGRAMMING
questions.learningObjective: Trace fall-through from default
questions.stem: In a multi-step plan, switch (x) { default: print("def"); case 1: print("one"); } with x=9 (no break), what prints?

options.text: "def" only because case 1 does not match.
"def" then "one" because default falls through to case 1.

questions.explanation: default runs for x=9 and, without break, falls through into case 1, printing "def" then "one".

questions.subject: JAVA_PROGRAMMING
questions.topic: Break Binds To The Inner Loop
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish break from a labelled break
questions.stem: In a loop containing a switch, an unlabelled break exits?

options.text: The innermost switch or loop, whichever encloses it most closely.
Nothing; break is invalid in a switch in a loop.

questions.explanation: break exits the nearest enclosing switch or loop. To target a specific outer construct, use a label.

questions.learningObjective: Avoid continue in a switch without a loop
questions.stem: Using continue inside a switch that is not inside a loop fails because?

options.text: continue is always valid in a switch.

questions.explanation: continue targets a loop. Without an enclosing loop, the compiler rejects it. Use break to exit the switch instead.

questions.topic: A Labelled Break Leaves The Switch
questions.learningObjective: Exit multiple nesting levels at once
questions.stem: A labelled break is most useful when you need to?

options.text: Skip one iteration of a loop.
Return a value from a method.
Exit an outer loop or block from deep inside nested constructs.

questions.explanation: A labelled break can exit any labelled enclosing construct, making it ideal for escaping deeply nested loops or switches.

questions.learningObjective: Avoid duplicate labels across cases
questions.stem: switch (x) { case 1 -> 10; case 1, 2 -> 20; } fails because?

options.text: Label 1 is duplicated across two cases.
Arrow labels cannot have multiple values.

questions.explanation: Each label value must appear in at most one case. Duplicating 1 across two cases is a compile error.
